investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) An act done by a British citizen or UK national in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom which would amount to this offence should it have been done committed in England and Wales, may be prosecuted under section 72.
(ii) A person guilty of this offence is subject to the notification and orders requirements as provided by Part 2 of this Act which commences at section 80. See also paragraph 17 of Schedule 3.
(iii) Officers should carefully check an offender's previous convictions. Provisions under sections 224 to 235 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 may mean that s/he is liable to receive a longer sentence if certain conditions apply.
(iv) A prior conviction for an offence listed in Schedule 15 to the Sentencing Act 2020, may render the convicted person liable to a mandatory life sentence in relation to a second offence listed under that Schedule, as per Section 273 (offender aged 18 or over but under 21 when convicted of the second offence or Section 283 (offender aged 21 or over).

other.penalty:
Indictable only - Life imprisonment

See Note (iv) above re mandatory life sentence
